subject: Private endpoint / egress & proxy qualification — next network asks
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@netsecure.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 17 May 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private endpoint / egress & proxy qualification — next network asks

Hi Alice — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the concrete asks we need to qualify the Private deployment path (PrivateLink / VPC peering / on-prem):

Summary (from our side)
- NetSecure is evaluating Private VPC deployment for tighter data residency and network controls. You flagged egress IPs, proxy usage, and whether PrivateLink or peering is preferred for your architecture.
- We covered traffic patterns (inference calls from app servers in your VPC to Redwood), and desire for tenant isolation and audit logging.

Action items / asks (please send items 1–4 before we schedule the technical deep-dive):
1) Preferred connectivity option: PrivateLink or VPC peering? If undecided, list any restrictions (no peering due to mesh policy, or PrivateLink only because of cross-account constraints).
2) Egress model: do you require fixed egress IPs for outbound traffic from Redwood to your services? If yes, provide any existing allowlist format (CIDR or single IP).
3) Proxy / TLS interception: Are outbound calls routed via a corporate proxy that performs TLS termination/inspection? If yes, share proxy hostname/IP and whether mTLS or client certs are required.
4) Controlled subnets: target subnet(s) and preferred AZs for endpoint creation (if using PrivateLink), or peering VPC ID and routing ownership notes.

Attachments: I attached our private connectivity checklist and an example egress IP list to help format items (redwood-privatelink-checklist.pdf, example-egress-ip-list.csv).

If you prefer, Laura and I can join your network ops call next week to walk through the checklist live. Proposed window: Tue 5/23 or Wed 5/24, 10–11am PT.

Thanks — feel free to reply inline.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com | +1 (415) 555-0129

From: Alice Wong <alice.wong@netsecure.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: ops-team@netsecure.io
Date: Thu, 17 May 2028 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint / egress & proxy qualification — next network asks

Thanks, Karthik — great summary. A few clarifications from NetSecure ops: 

- Connectivity: our security team prefers PrivateLink for third-party SaaS when possible; peering is allowed only for strategic partners after additional compliance review. So likely PrivateLink first.
- Egress: we do need a stable IP range for allowlisting outbound responses to some internal telemetry endpoints. A CSV with the exact CIDR(s) is perfect.
- Proxy: yes — our outbound traffic passes through an egress proxy that does TLS inspection. It is a forward proxy (no TLS termination for 3rd-party endpoints); we do not perform mTLS.
- Subnets: we can provide a list but will need Redwood to accept connections from cross-account PrivateLink endpoints into our service subnets in us-west-2.

We will pull the required items but two quick asks:
1) Is there a way to run a short network test (tcp/tls handshake) from Redwood to our proxy to validate routing?
2) If we choose PrivateLink, do you have any constraints around proxying the inbound traffic into your service (e.g., will PrivateLink health checks fail if traffic comes from a proxy IP)?

I'll aim to send the subnet/allowlist CSV tomorrow EOD. Can you confirm availability for the next-weekops call?

— Alice
Alice Wong
Head of Infrastructure | NetSecure
alice.wong@netsecure.io
[inline quoted Karthik's checklist omitted]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@netsecure.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 May 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint / egress & proxy qualification — next network asks

Alice — thanks, helpful. Short answers below, then a few more technical asks to make the deep-dive productive.

Quick answers:
- PrivateLink: fully supported and is our recommended path for SaaS customers who want strict inbound-only connectivity. We support cross-account NLB-based PrivateLink endpoints.
- Egress IPs: Redwood can provision a small set of stable egress IPs from our side for any callbacks or outbound webhook-style traffic — we will provide a CSV of the candidate IPs and can commit to a change-window for updates.
- Proxy: because your proxy is a forward TLS-inspecting proxy (no mTLS), that should be compatible. We do not expect PrivateLink health checks to fail because of proxying, but we need to validate the exact proxy behavior.

Additional technical asks (please supply as available):
A) Example HTTP(S) curl flow — sample hostname and any SNI or host header we should use.
B) Whether your proxy allows CONNECT tunneling for arbitrary hostnames (important for streaming responses).
C) ACLs on the target subnets (NACLs / Security Groups) — will you allow the PrivateLink ENIs and/or Redwood egress IPs?
D) Any DPI rules that drop long-lived streaming TCP connections (some inspection appliances close idle streams aggressively).

Attachments: redwood-vpc-arch.png (simple diagram of how PrivateLink + egress proxies interact).

If you can share A–D before our call, we'll prepare a short test plan and a validation script to run during the deep-dive. Proposed call times still Tue 5/23 10am PT or Wed 5/24 10am PT — Laura + Marissa can join.

Thanks — Karthik
[attachment: redwood-vpc-arch.png (PNG)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Re: Private endpoint / egress & proxy qualification — next network asks

Looping in a short ops note from our connectivity team: 

- If PrivateLink is used, we will create an internal NLB in our account and ask you to accept the endpoint. We typically request a small maintenance window (30–60 minutes) for the initial handshake and DNS failover updates.
- For egress IPs: we can provide up to 4 static IPv4 addresses for webhook callbacks. If you need IPv6, we can discuss but it's not part of our standard pattern today.
- Proxy handling: we can perform a quick synthetic test (curl with --proxy) during the call. If the proxy rewrites SNI/Host headers, we may ask your proxy team to allow the Redwood destination host header.

Laura Bennett
VP, Product Ops | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com
